canonical_name: Sabancı Vakfı — Gençlik Çalışmaları Akademisi (Youth Studies Academy)
notes: This is a capacity-building academy for adults who professionally work in the youth field (civil-society staff / 'gençlik çalışanları') — e.g. an open call selected 24 participants from 15 cities for 4 capacity-development trainings plus mentorship, explicitly aimed at strengthening organizations that work with young people, not at high-school students themselves. Not a fit for target #1.

canonical_name: Sabancı Vakfı — Fark Yaratanlar Programı (Changemakers Program)
notes: Real, long-running (17+ seasons) Sabancı Vakfı recognition/grant program for individuals, teams, projects, social enterprises, or institutions across environment/education/economic-development/health/social-justice/civic-participation themes. No explicit age floor was found in search-indexed content, but evaluation criteria require work that has 'moved beyond the idea stage, been implemented, and is currently ongoing' ('hayata geçirilmiş ve devam eden') — this is written for established civil-society/social-enterprise actors, not designed as or marketed toward high-school students, and we could not get a direct primary-source quote confirming or denying HS-age eligibility despite multiple search attempts. Not confidently recommendable as a target #1 fellowship for a 16-17 year old.

canonical_name: Koç Holding / Vehbi Koç Vakfı — Meslek Lisesi Memleket Meselesi (MLMM)
notes: Real, long-running (since 2006) Koç Holding/Vehbi Koç Vakfı project providing scholarships, internships, and volunteer coaching to vocational high school (meslek lisesi) students — but access is gated through 264 partner vocational schools (a student benefits only if their specific school is a partner), not an individually-applied national program. It is also specifically for the vocational-education track, a poor fit for ORYN's target user profile (a student preparing to apply to competitive universities abroad). Confirmed still referenced as active/current in 2026 discourse, but does not meet target #1's bar of an individually-accessible fellowship.

canonical_name: Koç Genç Yetenek Programı (Koç Young Talent Program)
notes: Career/talent program connecting Koç Holding with students; explicitly open to university students in their 2nd year and above (and graduate students), not high schoolers. Includes mentoring, volunteering with Koç managers, and AI training, but the age/education gate excludes ORYN's target user.

canonical_name: Garanti BBVA — 5 Taş Sosyal ve Finansal Liderlik Programı
notes: Developed with ÖRAV, this program develops social/financial leadership knowledge and skills, but is explicitly aimed at elementary and middle school students ('ilkokul ve ortaokul öğrencileri'), not high school age (14-18). Wrong age band for target #1.

canonical_name: Garanti BBVA — Genç Bankacılığı / Kariyerime İlk Adım / Kampüs Elçiliği
notes: Garanti BBVA's youth-branded programs (Genç Bankacılığı career track, Kariyerime İlk Adım free certified training, Kampüs Elçiliği ambassador program, Talent Camp internships) are all targeted at university students and new graduates preparing for banking careers, not high schoolers. The bank's only high-school-facing activity found was a one-off branch-visit financial literacy field trip (94 branches, 45 provinces, 2,400 students in a prior year) — a single field trip, not a multi-month fellowship.

canonical_name: TÜSİAD — Bu Gençlikte İŞ Var! (This Youth Has Business!)
notes: Directly fetched the official application page. 'Dönüşümü Başlat!' (idea competition) requires applicants aged 18-30; 'Dönüşümü Hızlandır!' (acceleration program) requires at least one founding partner aged 18-35. TÜSİAD's broader 'TÜSİAD Gençlik' arm is also explicitly a university-student working group (active since 2015). No high-school-eligible TÜSİAD youth program was found.

Under-20 program for young people already leading a social-impact project, no application fee. However, AYC currently only operates in the United States, Nigeria, Brazil, India, Bangladesh, and Indonesia — Turkey is not included, and the program explicitly states 'you can apply to Ashoka Young Changemakers (AYC) only in the country that you are a resident of.' Considered for target #2 (social entrepreneurship) but excluded on country grounds.

US-based program for female high school juniors who identify as African-American, Asian American, Latino, or Native American, attending a US public or parochial school, with household income under $125,000. Explicitly excludes a Turkey-based applicant on both demographic and country/school-system grounds. Considered for target #2, excluded.

Worldwide grants of $2,500-$15,000 for social-impact projects, but official eligibility explicitly requires applicants to be 18 years of age or older. Considered for target #2 (worldwide social-venture micro-grant), excluded on age grounds — this is exactly the kind of program The Pollination Project's lack of an age floor stands out against.
Youth-led service-project grants, but applicant organizations/individuals must be US-based. No international/Turkey eligibility found. Considered for target #2, excluded.

Age range 16-30 would otherwise fit a high schooler, but eligibility explicitly requires applicants to already be 'active members of a national, regional and/or global non-governmental and not-for-profit organization of youth and students working in a field related to SDG4.' Individual self-application without an existing qualifying organization membership is not possible — same structural problem as Wave 1's rejected 'Gençlik Projeleri Destekleme Programı' (applicant unit is an organization, not an individual). Considered for target #4, excluded.

canonical_name: Global Youth Biodiversity Network (GYBN) — Turkey/Europe chapter access [RE-CHECK, supersedes Wave 1 evidence]
notes: Fresh re-check with materially better evidence than Wave 1 (which was fully blocked at 403 on gybn.org). This time: (1) GYBN Europe's own site (a different, non-blocked Wix domain) was directly fetched and confirms Turkey is NOT among its named sub-regional chapters (Armenia, Austria, Italy, France, UK, Nordic countries, Western Balkans are named; Turkey is not). (2) Search-indexed content confirms general GYBN network membership has 'no minimum age to join,' BUT nearly all of its substantive programming — COP youth delegations, funded fellowships, election-eligible roles — requires ages 18-35, meaning a Turkey-based high schooler's realistic access reduces to passive network/mailing-list membership with no confirmed accessible substantive activity. gybn.org itself remained 403-blocked on this pass exactly as in Wave 1, confirming that block is a stable site characteristic, not a fluke. Net verdict is unchanged from Wave 1 (do not recommend) but now for a clearer, better-evidenced reason: not 'inaccessible/unconfirmed,' but 'technically joinable, not practically valuable for this age band, and no Turkey chapter exists.'

Fresh re-check. encodejustice.org still 301-redirects to encodeai.org (same as Wave 1 found — confirms this is a stable redirect, not a temporary migration glitch). NEW this pass: directly fetched encodeai.org itself and found zero references to 'Encode Justice,' no student chapters, no high-school/college program, and no youth-engagement pathway anywhere on the page — instead it presents a ~10-person professional AI-policy advocacy team based in San Francisco/DC with a generic adult-oriented 'get involved' contact form. A separate web search did surface an EFF article and a Harvard-hosted feed referencing an active 'Encode Justice NC' chapter with named student leaders, so SOME chapter activity may persist off the main domain (e.g. via Instagram/Discord rather than the website) — this could not be confirmed or denied further within budget. Net verdict: this looks like a genuine organizational wind-down/rebrand of the youth-chapter-facing website into an adult policy shop, not a resolvable site-migration hiccup, though a small residual chance of surviving chapters via non-web channels remains. Do not recommend as a citable, centrally-accessible program.

canonical_name: Rotary RYLA (Rotary Youth Leadership Awards) — Türkiye districts [RE-CHECK, supersedes Wave 1 evidence]
notes: Fresh re-check with materially better evidence. CONFIRMED currently active: a dated 2026-08-18 press article documents Rotary District 2440's 13th Group Clubs running a genuine 3-day RYLA at Izmir University of Economics in August 2026, ages 15-28 explicitly stated, covering environment/climate/disaster-awareness/AI/communication/leadership. This is fresher and more specific than anything Wave 1 had. HOWEVER, across 6 separate direct-fetch attempts this pass (District 2420's dedicated RYLA page x2, District 2430's RYLA page x2 plus a 'Ulusal RYLA' news-detail page, District 2440's guessed /ryla URL), every single one returned 404 or empty-nav content — none resolved to a working, fetchable eligibility/application page. A site: search of rotary2440.org additionally revealed WHY: District 2440 itself is organized as dozens of individual per-club subdomains (manisa.rotary2440.org, bornova.rotary2440.org, aydin.rotary2440.org, etc.) rather than one central district page, so RYLA content — when it exists — lives at the individual club/group level, not at a stable district URL. Net verdict unchanged from Wave 1 (no single citable official eligibility page), but this pass adds a structural explanation (bottom-up club-federated site architecture) for why that is genuinely hard to fix, not a research shortfall. A prospective student's real path is contacting a specific local Rotary club directly, not following a link.

canonical_name: The Diana Award — Development Programme (post-award benefit)
notes: Directly answers target #3's question for The Diana Award: YES, an ongoing post-award support programme for past Diana Award recipients does exist (curated opportunities list, a personal/professional development resource bank, monthly recipient newsletters, and inspiration content from fellow recipients; a separate, more intensive 6-month pilot programme was also found scoped specifically to recipients 'across Africa,' which would not reach a Turkey-based recipient). Recorded here as a REJECTED/no-new-record entry — not because it doesn't exist, but because it is not an independently-accessible opportunity: eligibility is 'Now that you are a Diana Award recipient, you have access to...' i.e. it is a bundled benefit gated entirely behind already winning the Diana Award itself, which Wave 1 already has on file as its own VERIFIED record (nomination-gated). Flagging here so a future researcher doesn't re-spend budget chasing this as if it were a separate, directly-applicable opportunity — recommend instead adding this as an enrichment note on the existing Diana Award record.
